Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Dialysis patients with depressive symptoms had significantly lower serum vitamin D levels than those without.
Sentence: "Patients with depressive symptoms have significantly higher serum HsCRP level and significantly lower serum VD level compared with the control group."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (BDI)
Population: 484 chronic dialysis patients (382 hemodialysis, 102 peritoneal dialysis) aged 18-60 in southeast China
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (VD2 + VD3) measured at baseline
Comparator: Dialysis patients without depressive symptoms (BDI <16)
Design: case series
Sample size: 484
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D3 levels were statistically significantly associated with depression (BDI-II) among rural adolescents; direction not reported.
Sentence: "There was a statistically significant association between depression and Vitamin D3 levels."
Measured as: depression (Beck's Depression Inventory-II)
Population: 451 rural adolescents aged 11-18 years in government high schools in Kolar, India, excluding those with pre-existing mental illness
Intervention: Measured serum vitamin D3 level (25-OH total), no intervention
Comparator: Adolescents with sufficient vitamin D levels versus insufficient and deficient levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 451
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational vitamin D level studies on depression, but Study B is labelled 'no effect' while its own sentence reports a significant association (direction unreported), so the findings do not truly conflict.","verdict":"apparent","reason":"outcome_measure","also_differs":["population","design_or_bias"],"detail":"Study B's 'no effect' label conflicts with its reported significant association, direction unreported; Study A is dialysis adults with a BDI cut-off, Study B is healthy rural adolescents on BDI-II"}
